external_entities.name: user's browser
external_entities.description: A user's browser that communicates with the web application.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

processes.name: web application
processes.description: The web application receives browser traffic, enqueues jobs, and reads its configuration.
processes.source_excerpt: The web application does not do the heavy work itself. It puts jobs onto a message queue

processes.name: background worker
processes.description: A background worker process that picks up jobs and performs the work, including reading and writing the database.
processes.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.

data_stores.name: message queue
data_stores.description: A queue where the web application puts jobs and the background worker picks them up.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue, and a background worker process picks them up

data_stores.name: database
data_stores.description: The database read and written by the background worker; it also stores the application's log records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The database is also where we keep the application's log records.

data_stores.name: web application config
data_stores.description: The configuration store for the web application, holding the credentials it needs for the queue.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web application has a web application config

data_stores.name: worker config
data_stores.description: The configuration store for the worker, holding the credentials it needs for the database.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config

data_flows.name: talks to
data_flows.description: The user's browser communicates with the web application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

data_flows.name: puts jobs
data_flows.description: The web application puts jobs onto the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue

data_flows.name: picks up jobs
data_flows.description: The background worker picks jobs up from the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up

data_flows.name: reads and writes
data_flows.description: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database.

data_flows.name: reads settings
data_flows.description: The web application reads its settings from its configuration store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: the web application has a web application config

data_flows.name: reads settings
data_flows.description: The background worker reads its settings from its configuration store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: … the worker has a worker config

trust_boundaries.name: outside our network
trust_boundaries.description: The network area outside the organisation's network where the user's browser sits.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The browser sits outside our network

trust_boundaries.name: web tier
trust_boundaries.description: The tier where the web application runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the web application runs in our web tier.

trust_boundaries.name: backend tier
trust_boundaries.description: The backend tier containing the queue, worker, and database behind the web tier.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The queue, the worker and the database are all in the backend tier, behind the web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The web application is internet-facing because a user's browser reaches it across the public internet.
assumptions.basis: The source states that a user's browser talks to the web application across the public internet.

assumptions.assumption: The background worker presents a non-web interface because it is described as a background worker process rather than a web application.
assumptions.basis: The source describes it as a background worker process that picks up jobs and does work.

assumptions.assumption: The web application config is confidential because it holds the web application's queue credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the web application config holds the credentials the process needs.

assumptions.assumption: The worker config is confidential because it holds the worker's database credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the worker config holds the credentials the process needs.

assumptions.assumption: The outside our network, web tier, and backend tier boundaries are network boundaries because the source distinguishes them as network locations.
assumptions.basis: The source places the browser outside our network.

assumptions.assumption: The web tier is a network boundary because the source distinguishes it from the backend tier.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the web application runs in the web tier and that the backend tier is behind it.

assumptions.assumption: The backend tier is a network boundary because the source distinguishes it from the web tier.
assumptions.basis: The source places the queue, worker, and database in the backend tier behind the web tier.
